title: TypedEmitter: adversarial-resilience and compatibility validation harness for constrained decoders
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible test harness (TypedEmitter) that stresses constrained decoders across adversarial payloads, partial-stream interrupts, and tool-calling interleaving to validate compatibility policies and graceful degradation behavior.

Scope:
- Exercise constrained-decoding modes for canonical typed outputs (JSON-like canonical payloads) across streaming and non-streaming endpoints.
- Simulate deliberate mis-emits (extra commas, truncated objects, stray tokens) and measure decoder recovery, backoff, and fallback rates.
- Validate interaction with tool/function-calls: ensure sentinel encoding and tool-call return schema remain decodable after partial emits and retransmits.
- Verify compatibility layer behavior when falling back to permissive decoders or model-variant routing.

Test matrix (high level):
- Input families: well-formed schema, off-by-one commas, large KV cache influence, prefix truncated at 10/30/70% completion, injected toolcall tokens mid-object.
- Models: small (latency baseline), medium, and large (regression target). Use quantized variants where available.
- Modes: streaming chunked partials, streaming with token drop (simulate network loss), non-stream strict decode.
- Policies: strict-enforce -> reject, soft-enforce -> accept with sanitization, fallback-route -> route to permissive variant.

Metrics captured:
- decodes_per_hour, strict_reject_rate, sanitized_accept_rate, average_recovery_latency_ms, tokens_emitted_before_recovery, number_of_toolcall_disruptions, telemetry_tags (model, route, policy, commit).

Acceptance criteria:
1) For the baseline model under strict-enforce, malformed inputs should be rejected >= 98% of the time without crashing the runtime.
2) For soft-enforce, sanitizer should successfully canonicalize malformed payloads into schema-compliant outputs for >= 90% of generated responses within 200ms median additional latency.
3) Streaming partial-truncate scenarios should prefer a deterministic reassembly path and produce either a valid payload or a clear reject/error sentinel (no silent corruption).
4) Tool/function calling interleaving tests must demonstrate that tool-return payloads are preserved or safely rolled back with explicit error markers in >= 99% of trials.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Harness runner: a new binary under infra/testtools/typed_emitter_runner that drives model endpoints and injects adversarial patterns.
- SDK hooks: extend streaming SDK test doubles to allow simulated token loss and mid-stream injections.
- Observability: add metrics to console-telemetry (metric names in the harness README).
- CI: add a nightly matrix job gated under runtime-1.20 that fails PRs if strict-enforce regression observed (>1%).

Notes & trade-offs:
- We intentionally avoid a single canonical sanitizer implementation; the harness will allow multiple sanitizer strategies so PM/Research can experiment.
- Running full adversarial matrix is compute heavy; we'll start with a representative seed set and scale to wide matrix in the nightly bucket.
